$comment: Permutation source for x-tooltip. Params and values come from src/wb-models/tooltip.schema.json -- every declared property, its enum, its default, plus min/max/edge values the enum does not state. Tests are GENERATED from this file; none are hand-picked.

simpleWorkingCase.expect: a tooltip element appears containing the text 'hello', and disappears when the pointer leaves

values: a very long string of 400 characters used to test maxWidth wrapping

delay.note: tooltip.js clamps with Math.max(0, parseInt(...)). -50 and 'abc' are the min/invalid edges.

hideDelay.note: Was a disagreement: tooltip.schema.json said 0, tooltip.js used 100. Reconciled to 100 in #1107 -- it is the shipped behaviour, and it is the value interactive=true needs, so the pointer can cross the 8px gap onto the tooltip before it hides.

trigger.note: Was DECLARED, NEVER READ: tooltip.js bound mouseenter, mouseleave and focus always, so click never opened the tooltip and hover always did. #1107 gates the listeners per mode -- hover binds mouseenter/mouseleave, focus binds focus/blur, click binds click alone (neither hover nor focus) and toggles, hover-focus binds both. Default reconciled to hover-focus (#1107): focus was always bound before gating, and dropping it would remove keyboard access (WCAG 1.4.13).

arrow.note: Was DECLARED, NEVER READ: tooltip.js built .x-tooltip__arrow unconditionally, so arrow=false could not remove it. #1107 builds the arrow only when the flag is on.

interactive.note: Was DECLARED, NEVER READ: no pointer-bridge logic existed, and .x-tooltip is pointer-events:none, so the pointer could never reach the tooltip anyway. #1107 adds .x-tooltip--interactive (pointer-events:auto) and cancels the pending hide when the pointer enters the tooltip.

maxWidth.note: Was DECLARED, NEVER READ: the cap was a hardcoded 250px in the injected CSS. #1107 sets the declared --x-tooltip-max-width CSS API variable per instance on a border-box element, so the cap means the rendered width. A 0px cap still renders the padding box -- padding cannot shrink.

rule: content: the tooltip's text equals the authored content exactly; markup in it is text, never parsed as HTML.

content empty or whitespace-only: falls through to the trigger's own text, which #861 made the last content source on purpose so the bare <button x-tooltip>Save</button> form works. Only a trigger with no text at all has nothing to say.
position: the tooltip carries .x-tooltip--<position> AND sits on that side of the trigger, measured by rect.
position: the 4 compound values (top-start/top-end/bottom-start/bottom-end) must place the tooltip too -- tooltip.js only styles the 4 simple sides.
variant: each of the 4 values paints a visually distinct tooltip; two variants may not be pixel-identical.
delay: the tooltip does not appear before `delay` ms and does appear after; delay=0 appears immediately.
delay invalid or negative: clamped to 0, never NaN and never a permanent no-show.
hideDelay: the tooltip survives at least `hideDelay` ms after the pointer leaves, then goes.
trigger: the tooltip opens on the named interaction AND NOT on the others.
arrow=false: no .x-tooltip__arrow element; arrow=true: exactly one.
interactive=true: moving the pointer from trigger onto the tooltip keeps it open.
maxWidth: the rendered tooltip's width never exceeds the value.
every permutation: exactly one .x-tooltip exists while shown, and it is removed from the DOM on hide -- none may leak.
expectedRedOnCurrentCode: trigger=click: never opens on click, and wrongly opens on hover/focus
trigger=focus / hover-focus: indistinguishable from hover, since all three are always bound
arrow=false: the arrow is built unconditionally (tooltip.js:181-185)
maxWidth: never applied to the built element
hideDelay default disagreement: schema says 0, tooltip.js defaults to 100
position compound values: only top/bottom/left/right have arrow/placement CSS
oracle.resolvedIn: #1107 -- every case listed in expectedRedOnCurrentCode is now expected GREEN. The list stays as written: it is the definition of done for that fix and the record of what was wrong.
